messages.subject: Censored gaussian using inla.surv
parts:
Hello, suppose I have a Gaussian data generating process:
```
Y ~ Normal(\mu, \sigma)
```

but I only observe

```
Z ~ max(Y, c)
```

where c is my left censor point. I tried using inla.surv to do inference (for parameters mu, sigma) but I guess this is not the intended use. Any ideas how to fit this model in INLA?

Here is some fake data:
```
N=1000 # sample size
mu = 0    # true mean
sigma = 5 # true sd

Y = rnorm(N, mean=mu, sd=sigma) # observations
c = -1 # left censor point

Z = sapply(Y, max, c) # censored observations
```

Attempt to fit the model with INLA's `inla.surv` as follows:
```
event = sapply(Y, function(x) if(x < c) 2 else 1)
df = data.frame(Z, event)   
formula = inla.surv(Z, event) ~ 1
imod = inla(formula, family="gaussian", data=df, verbose=TRUE)
```

I get the following error:
```
Error in inla.surv.1(time, event, time2, truncation) :
  Negative times are not allowed 
```

Out of curiosity I also tried changing the left censor point to a positive number (e.g., L=1) and then I get a different error:

```
*** ERROR ***     inla_read_data_likelihood: file [/tmp/RtmpZcvs0y/file6d3c7840907c/data.files/file6d3c518a7068] contains [7000] elements, which is not a multiple of [3]

Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.
```

I attached the output when `verbose=TRUE`.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Censored gaussian using inla.surv
parts:
Hi,

the normal is not implemented as a survival model, but the lognormal
is, see inla.doc("lognormal")

can you use that one instead?

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Censored gaussian using inla.surv
parts:
Thanks for the quick reply. Lognormal is fine for my purposes. I changed my code to generate data with `rlnorm` and used family="lognormalsurv" in INLA:

```
N=10000 # sample size
mu = 1    # true mean
sigma = .5 # true sd

Y = rlnorm(N, mean=mu, sd=sigma)
c = 5 # left censor point
Z = sapply(Y, max, c)

event = sapply(Y, function(x) if(x < c) 0 else 1)
hist(Y)
hist(Z)

df = data.frame(Z, event)   
formula = inla.surv(Z, event) ~ 1

imod = inla(formula, family="lognormal.surv", data=df, verbose=TRUE)
```

The problem is that the inference is off:

```
Fixed effects:
              mean     sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode kld
(Intercept) 1.2447 0.0127     1.2198   1.2446     1.2697 1.2446   0
```

This is my first time using INLA. Have I made a mistake?

I have attached the full output of summary(imod) and also the verbose output of the inla fit. For reference I attached an equivalent model in Stan, where the parameters are successfully recovered. Thanks!

Nevermind, I was coding the event wrong. It should be:
```
event = sapply(Y, function(x) if(x < c) 2 else 1)

Now I get:

Fixed effects:
              mean    sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant   mode kld

(Intercept) 1.0104 0.016      0.979   1.0104     1.0418 1.0104   0
```

Thanks!
